To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Comt+ allele contains a miRNA signal that is absent in the ComtB2 allele; (2) this signal is responsible for Comt+ transcript degradation; and (3) this miRNA signal is responsible for the increased COMT activity levels in ComtB2 mice.

the ComtB2 allele has higher Comt expression levels than the ancestral allele due to an early polyadenylate signal introduced by the B2 element, which leads to a shorter mRNA lacking regulatory miRNA signals.
the insertion of a short interspersed element in the mouse catecholl-O-methyltransferas gene 3′-UTR introduces a new early polyadenylation site, which leads to a shorter transcript.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic mechanisms that regulate the expression of the mouse Comt gene.
the functional consequences of the B2 short intersperse element insertion in the mouse Comt locus.
the molecular genetic mechanisms of allelo-specific regulation of the mouse Comt gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the insertion of the B2 repeat element in the 3′-UTR of the mouse Comt gene results in a shorter Comt mRNA that lacks miRNA binding sites, leading to higher Comt mRNA stability and increased Comt enzymatic activity.

the ComtB2 allele is a functional polymorphism that leads to increased COMT activity and that this is due to the insertion of an early polyadenylating signal that generates a shorter Comt mRNA that is less susceptible to degradation by miRNAs.

the insertion of the B2 repeat in the 3′UTR of the mouse Comt gene leads to the generation of a shorter transcript, which does not contain the miRNAs signals present in the 3’UTR of the ancestral transcript, leading to higher mRNA expression and enzymatic activity of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insertion of the B2 short interspaced element into the Comt+ gene is responsible for the allelic specific regulation and the phenotypic differences between ComtB2 and Comt+ mice.
the insertion of the B2 short intersperse element in the 3′-UTR of the Comt gene results in the production of a shorter transcript that lacks the regulatory signals of the ancestral transcript.

the B2 insertion into the Comt 3′-UTR has a dual effect on Comt mRNA expression: on the one hand, it introduces a premature polyadenylation signal, resulting in the generation of a shorter transcript; on the other hand, it eliminates the miRNA binding sites, resulting in higher expression of the longer transcript.
The main takeaway from our work is that
allelic specific regulation is a common feature of the Comt gene and that the ancestral allele is under stronger transcriptional control than the functional allele.
the Comt B2 element insertion has a functional effect on Comt mRNA levels, leading to increased COMT activity and altered phenotypes in ComtB2 mice.
the ComtB2 insertion is a genetic mechanism that increases Comt expression by removing regulatory miRNA binding sites.
